description: Baseline: random init, prints the public task attributes to learn vocab and prompt format.
4 layers no LayerNorm: '=' is a CPU; two heads read op_L and bit_L, third loads b0, MLP is a 4-rule transition table on a state register.
One block with shared weights clocked 4 times; a program-counter register steers attention to (op_L, bit_L) and the MLP advances it.
Read-only tape via causal cross-attention, transient reads, one head fetching (op,bit) pairs, 5 clocks with '=' read as '|'; 4 rules + 5 counter units.
E03 with the program counter stored in the position dims: the '=' position embedding is the boot state, so d_model falls from 22 to 17.
Scalar pointer C addresses the tape via parabolic attention -(p-C)^2/2, moving +2 per clock; 3 state rules + 1 clock unit, d_model 9, d_ff 4.
Attention reduced to a query map (no W_k W_v W_o); tape is keys and values; pointer lives in the position dim and moves +4 per clock; d_model 8.
E06 at attention sharpness beta=1: control measuring how hard the read must be.
E06 at attention sharpness beta=3: brackets the threshold for exact reads.
E06 at attention sharpness beta=2: narrows the threshold between beta=1 (fails) and beta=3 (exact).
Clock moved from a hidden unit into fc2.bias, so d_ff is exactly the 3 rewrite rules; beta=10.
Token '=' embedded identically to '|', dropping the EQ dim; d_model 7, d_ff 3.
Operators coded in two bits (& = U, | = V, ^ = U+V), so one wire covers 'op in {|,^}'; d_model 6, d_ff 3.
Position table trimmed from 16 to the 10 prompt cells; no unused embedding rows remain.
Causal mask removed: the CPU sits at the last cell, so no future cell exists for it and the mask should be dead code.
Operators on one scalar wire (&=0, |=1, ^=2): d_model 5 but d_ff 4, trading a clean rule table for fewer parameters.
Control: E15 with 4 clocks instead of 5, so the last (op, bit) is never applied; expected to fail.
Control: E15 with 6 clocks, pushing the pointer past the end of the tape; tests whether the machine halts cleanly.
Robustness: E15 with a fixed Gaussian perturbation of std 0.01 on every parameter (no fitting).
Tests the tie-fragility hypothesis: same std 0.01 noise as E18 with softer attention (beta=3 instead of 10).
Removes the attention tie: two heads each peak on an integer cell (op, bit); same std 0.01 noise as E18 at beta=10.
E20 without noise: confirms the two-head design is itself correct, separating a broken design from a fragile one.
Tests the amplification hypothesis: a fixed mask stops address dims (up to 32) reaching the MLP; same std 0.01 noise and seed as E20.
Tests the peak-drift hypothesis: curvature and head offset come from W_q biases instead of a noisy stored register; same std 0.01 noise and seed.
Tests the error-amplification hypothesis: two-bit opcode rules have coefficient +-1 on S, so firing overwrites S; d_model 6, d_ff 3, same std 0.01 noise.
Replication: E24 with noise seed 1 instead of 0, checking the robustness gain was not a lucky draw.
Ablation: E25 without the key/value mask (same noise seed 1), measuring whether the mask earns its place in the robust design.
Breakdown point: robust design (mask restored) at noise std 0.03, three times E25, seed 1.
Checks whether the integer rescale kept the robustness: E28 at noise std 0.01, seed 1 (compare E25).
Brackets the breakdown point of the final integer design: noise std 0.02, seed 1.
Final clean candidate: robust two-head tape machine with every weight a small integer (keys (p,-p^2)); d_model 6, d_ff 3, no noise.
